key_concept: Solanaceae floral formula: $\oplus\, ⚥\, K_{(5)}\, \widehat{C_{(5)}\, A_5}\, \underline{G}_{(2)}$. The flowers are bisexual and actinomorphic, with five united sepals, five united petals, five epipetalous stamens and a superior bicarpellary syncarpous ovary.
steps: Recall the floral formula of Solanaceae: $\oplus\, ⚥\, K_{(5)}\, \widehat{C_{(5)}\, A_5}\, \underline{G}_{(2)}$.
Statement (a): The flowers are bisexual ($⚥$) and actinomorphic ($\oplus$). Correct.
Statement (b): The calyx has five sepals that are united (gamosepalous, $K_{(5)}$), and it is persistent. Correct.
Statement (c): The androecium has five stamens attached to the petals (epipetalous). In the formula this is shown by the arc joining $C$ and $A$. Correct.
Statement (d): The ovary is superior, as shown by the line below $G$ in $\underline{G}_{(2)}$. It is not inferior, so this statement is incorrect.
Therefore only (a), (b) and (c) are correct, which matches option (1).
why_not_others: Options (2) and (4) include (d), but the Solanaceae ovary is superior, not inferior. Option (3) leaves out (c), even though the stamens in Solanaceae are epipetalous.
common_trap: Students confuse the ovary position with Compositae (Asteraceae), where the ovary is inferior, and wrongly mark (d) as correct.
time_saving_tip: Spot that (d) is false because the Solanaceae ovary is superior. This removes options (2) and (4). Then confirm that (c) is true, which leaves option (1).
